text:
discard
Description
Causes the current packet or connection (depending on the context of
the event) to be dropped/discarded and the rule continues (no implied
return). This command is identical to
drop
.
Syntax
discard
discard
Causes the current packet or connection (depending on the context of
the event) to be discarded. Nothing is sent to the client.
Removes the corresponding entry from the system connection table.
Note that, in the case of TCP, if subsequent segments arrive without
SYN bit set (and ACK bit unset), a RST will be sent as a result. This
is the standard behavior when segments of that type arrive when there
is no system connection entry.
Examples
when
SERVER_CONNECTED
{
if
{
[
IP
::
addr
[
IP
::
client_addr
]
equals
10.1
.1.80
]
}
{
discard
log
local0.
"connection discarded from [IP::client_addr]"
}
}
After “discard” is executed, the rule will continue until the end of
the current event so “connection discarded …” will be logged.
Related Information
Valid Events:
ALL_EVENTS
